scope_note: Backfill edition from arXiv /pastweek date sections. The repo parser found 98 cs.CV rows and 36 cs.RO rows; after deduplication, 127 papers remained and 58 were ROI. Tier A cards use official arXiv abstract pages plus available arXiv HTML headings, and avoid claiming PDF-only evidence.
executive_thesis: The August 3 backfill is about replacing generic VLA scaling with state-aware policy repair. WCM asks whether the critic should see temporal robot history, RayViT injects camera rays before imitation breaks under viewpoint shift, ST-WAM separates action-relevant future state from visual hallucination, and CorrelationFlow rejects the common LiDAR scene-flow formulation when sparse or fast objects violate its assumptions. APRL should treat viewpoint, temporal history, and failure geometry as separate audit axes before adding more robot demonstrations.

decision_cards.label: Decision
decision_cards.title: Critics need robot history, not only current-frame features
decision_cards.body: WCM frames single-frame critic latents as a mismatch for partially observable robot control. That pushes APRL toward value diagnostics that condition on recent observation, action, and state transitions.

decision_cards.label: Decision
decision_cards.title: Viewpoint robustness is a geometry interface problem
decision_cards.body: RayViT does not just add more augmentation; it gives the visual backbone camera-ray structure. A VLA robustness run should ablate geometry encoding separately from data volume.

decision_cards.label: Decision
decision_cards.title: World-action models must preserve task state under visual shift
decision_cards.body: ST-WAM identifies training-distribution hallucination in visually shifted futures. Future prediction is useful for control only when it keeps the state that changes the action.

papers.title: WCM: A World Critic Model for Vision-Language-Action Reinforcement Learning
papers.fit: VLA reinforcement learning - temporal critic - partially observable control
papers.status: Tier A - official arXiv abstract and HTML structure checked
papers.status_quo: VLA RL post-training often attaches a critic to current visual state or current VLM latents.
papers.friction: Robot manipulation is partially observable; a single frame can miss the causal state that explains success or failure.
papers.hidden_premise: A useful critic must compress recent world history without exploding the visual-state complexity.
papers.conceptual_move: Treat the value estimator as a world critic that reasons over temporally grounded robot state.
papers.mechanism: The official abstract motivates history-aware critic modeling for VLA RL instead of a single-frame value head.

evidence.claim: The paper explicitly calls single-frame critic observations a mismatch for partially observable robot control.
The official arXiv HTML exposes Methodology and Experiments sections for the world critic formulation.
The reusable APRL variable is critic state history, not a larger policy backbone.

papers.falsification: If history-aware critics do not improve under occlusion, delayed reward, or contact ambiguity, the claimed world-state benefit is weak.
papers.adversarial: A history critic can overfit benchmark progress signals unless evaluated on held-out failure families.
papers.thinking_tool: Before RL post-training, decide which unobserved state the critic must remember and how to ablate it.
papers.transfer_boundary: Best for multi-step manipulation and delayed-contact tasks; weaker for single-step pick tasks with full observability.

papers.title: RayViT: Ray-Conditioned Visual Representations for Viewpoint-Robust Imitation Learning
papers.fit: viewpoint-robust imitation - camera geometry - visual representation
papers.status: Tier A - official arXiv abstract and HTML structure checked
papers.status_quo: Imitation policies trained from RGB often absorb camera viewpoint as an untyped nuisance.
papers.friction: RGB lacks explicit geometric cues, so policies become brittle when camera pose shifts.
papers.hidden_premise: The perception backbone should know the camera ray geometry before it maps pixels to action state.
papers.conceptual_move: Inject Plucker ray maps into a pretrained ViT with gated cross-attention.
papers.mechanism: Ray features condition image patches, making viewpoint part of the representation rather than a hidden dataset bias.

evidence.claim: The paper names RGB-only camera perturbation brittleness and proposes a ray-conditioned ViT encoder.
Official HTML includes simulated and real robot experiment sections.
APRL should compare ray-conditioned encoders against viewpoint augmentation at equal data size.

papers.falsification: If ray conditioning helps only on synthetic camera shifts but not real robot camera recalibration, it is not a robust interface.
papers.adversarial: Camera geometry can be miscalibrated; the robustness claim needs calibration-error stress splits.
papers.thinking_tool: Expose camera geometry as a typed policy input before collecting more viewpoint-diverse demos.
papers.transfer_boundary: Strong for multi-camera and mobile manipulation; less direct when proprioception or tactile state dominates.

papers.title: ST-WAM: Semantic-Temporal World Action Model for Robust Manipulation under Visual Distribution Shifts
papers.fit: world-action model - visual shift - manipulation robustness
papers.status: Tier A - official arXiv abstract and HTML structure checked
papers.status_quo: WAMs often supervise future pixels and actions together, assuming generated futures preserve control-relevant state.
papers.friction: Under visual distribution shift, generated futures can hallucinate training-domain content rather than the actual shifted scene.
papers.hidden_premise: The future state useful for action is semantic-temporal, not every visual detail in the predicted frame.
papers.conceptual_move: Separate action-relevant future state from task-irrelevant visual content in WAM supervision.
papers.mechanism: The abstract identifies Training-Distribution Hallucination and motivates a semantic-temporal WAM for robust manipulation.

evidence.claim: The authors describe WAM future supervision entangling action-relevant transitions with irrelevant visual content.
Official HTML includes Methodology and Experiments sections.
The key APRL audit is whether the generated future preserves the state that changes action choice.

papers.falsification: If shifted futures look wrong but action success remains unchanged, visual hallucination is not the operational failure.
papers.adversarial: A semantic-temporal loss can still hide force, contact, and object-state errors.
papers.thinking_tool: Evaluate WAMs by action-state preservation under controlled visual shifts.
papers.transfer_boundary: Useful for visually shifted manipulation; less complete for contact-rich tasks without force channels.

papers.title: CorrelationFlow: A Training-Free Geometric Approach for LiDAR Scene Flow Estimation
papers.fit: LiDAR scene flow - geometric formulation - sparse moving objects
papers.status: Tier A - official arXiv abstract and HTML structure checked
papers.status_quo: Recent LiDAR scene-flow methods share feed-forward architectures and self-supervised losses.
papers.friction: Those assumptions fail together for sparse, distant, or fast-moving objects.
papers.hidden_premise: When a formulation fails, adding parameters or simulated data may not repair the geometric blind spot.
papers.conceptual_move: Use a training-free geometric approach to scene flow instead of another learned variant of the same template.
papers.mechanism: The official abstract frames the method as a deliberate escape from shared architectural monoculture.

evidence.claim: The paper names sparse, distant, and fast-moving object failures as shared blind spots.
Official HTML includes CorrelationFlow, component, and keypoint sections.
APRL should keep a classical geometric baseline in dynamic-map evaluations.

papers.falsification: If learned baselines recover under matched sparse-object stress, the formulation critique is overstated.
papers.adversarial: Training-free geometry can be brittle under sensor noise, rain, or severe ego-motion.
papers.thinking_tool: When a whole method family fails together, change the problem formulation before scaling it.
papers.transfer_boundary: Direct for LiDAR flow and map update; indirect for RGB-only SLAM.

synthesis.title: State variables are becoming the real comparison unit
synthesis.facts: The papers each introduce a missing state channel: temporal critic history, camera rays, or semantic-temporal future state.
synthesis.inference: APRL should compare policies by which hidden state they expose and ablate, not by backbone family.

synthesis.title: Geometry remains a counterweight to learned monoculture
synthesis.facts: The 3D/Scene bucket includes LiDAR scene flow, active reconstruction entropy, and Gaussian gap filling.
synthesis.inference: A robot map benchmark should include geometric failure cases before accepting generated or learned map updates.

frontier_memory.label: Strengthening
frontier_memory.history: Late July already emphasized WAM state channels.
frontier_memory.body: August 3 adds critic history and camera-ray geometry as typed interfaces.

frontier_memory.label: Missing axis
frontier_memory.body: Force/contact uncertainty remains under-specified in the WAM papers selected today.

strategy.title: Typed-state VLA audit harness
strategy.thesis: Measure whether temporal history, camera geometry, and generated future state independently change action success.
strategy.one_week: Run one policy with camera-ray on/off, critic-history on/off, and shifted-background WAM probes.
strategy.four_week: Build a reusable typed-state benchmark for VLA and WAM failures.
strategy.success: At least one state channel predicts a held-out failure family better than a generic confidence score.
strategy.stop: No channel changes failure prediction or recovery under controlled stress.
strategy.asset: Typed-state audit schema plus small stress-suite videos.
